### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls

`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > The `?favorited=` filter compares the wrong column
**What happened:** `findAll()` collects the ids of the articles a user favourited and then
filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` — the article ids are being compared to author ids. Even
once the `favorites` relation is loaded, the result is wrong.

**Rule:** when a filter is "articles in this set", the column is `article.id`. Read the
`andWhere` literally; do not trust the variable name.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Static routes are declared before parameterised ones (#7)
**What happened:** `GET /articles/feed` was declared *after* `GET /articles/:slug`, so Nest
matched `feed` as a slug and the feed endpoint returned `{ article: undefined }`. Fixed by moving
`getFeed()` above `findOne()` in `ArticleController`.

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > An invalid token must be a 401, not a 500 (#79)
**What happened:** an expired or tampered token made `jwt.verify()` throw inside
`AuthMiddleware.use()` (and inside the `@User()` decorator on public routes). Nothing caught it,
so the client got `500 Internal Server Error` and the mobile app treated it as an outage instead
of logging the user out.

**Rule:** wrap `jwt.verify` and translate its errors to `HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED`. A guard that
can crash is a guard that leaks framework errors.

runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

text:
**Refined prompt:** Diagnose why the React client throws `Cannot read property 'slug' of undefined` immediately after article creation while the NestJS server logs nothing — answering as a backend engineer on this RealWorld API, citing the failing line as `file:line`, fixing at the single source rather than patching consumers, and reporting blast radius plus a verification step.

## Root cause

`src/article/article.service.ts:170` and `:186` — `create()` is the one handler in the codebase that returns a **bare entity instead of the `{ article }` envelope**:

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts:170
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleEntity> {
  ...
  return newArticle;     // :186  ← flat entity
}
```

`src/article/article.controller.ts:52` passes it straight through and — unlike its siblings at `:25`, `:34`, `:39`, `:44` — carries **no `Promise<ArticleRO>` annotation**, so TypeScript never flagged the mismatch:

```ts
// src/article/article.controller.ts:52
async create(@User('id') userId: number, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto) {
```

So `POST /api/articles` responds `{"id":1,"slug":"foo-x7k2p1",...}` where every other article endpoint responds `{"article":{...}}` (`article.service.ts:98`, `:111`, `:144`, `:194`). The client reads `response.article.slug`; `response.article` is `undefined`.

**Why the server logs nothing:** nothing threw. The insert succeeded, Nest returned `201`, and the request is a clean success from the server's side. The defect lives entirely in the *shape* of a successful response — invisible to logs, invisible to Postman if you only eyeball the fields.

## The fix

One place — the service, matching every sibling method. The controller annotation is what makes the compiler enforce it going forward.

```diff
--- a/src/article/article.service.ts
@@ -170,7 +170,7 @@
-  async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleEntity> {
+  async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
@@ -186,1 +186,1 @@
-    return newArticle;
+    return {article: newArticle};

--- a/src/article/article.controller.ts
@@ -52,1 +52,1 @@
-  async create(@User('id') userId: number, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto) {
+  async create(@User('id') userId: number, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
```

`ArticleRO` is already imported in both files (`article.service.ts:10`, `article.controller.ts:5`). I have no file-edit tool in this session, so **I have not applied this** — say the word and I'll write it via the shell.

## Blast radius

- **Only `POST /api/articles` changes shape.** I checked every article handler: `update`, `createComment`, `deleteComment`, `favorite`, `unFavorite` (`controller.ts:60,77,85,94,102`) also lack return annotations, but their services already return `{article}` — annotation debt, not runtime bugs. `delete()` returns a `DeleteResult`; the spec expects no body there.
- **No consumer depends on the flat shape** — today it crashes every client that calls it, so there is nothing to migrate.
- **No test covers it.** The only spec file in the repo is `src/tag/tag.controller.spec.ts`.

## Two things this fix does *not* solve

1. **`create()` never sets `body`** — `article.service.ts:172-177` assigns `title`, `description`, `slug`, `tagList`, `comments` and skips `body`, even though `CreateArticleDto` declares it (`dto/create-article.dto.ts:4`) and the column defaults to `''` (`article.entity.ts:20-21`). **Existing data is already wrong:** every article created through this API has an empty body, silently, and no error was ever raised. Backfill isn't possible — the text was never persisted.
2. **`author` is absent from the response.** `newArticle` is the pre-relation save; `authorId` only gets written by the inverse-side save at `:181-184`, and the returned object carries no `author`. So `article.author.username` is your next `undefined` read — and `findOne()` (`:96-99`) doesn't join the author either, so the redirect to the article page won't rescue it.

Both are in scope-adjacent code I deliberately left alone. Tell me if you want them.

## How to verify

```powershell
$t = "<jwt>"
$r = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri http://localhost:3000/api/articles `
  -Headers @{Authorization="Token $t"; "Content-Type"="application/json"} `
  -Body '{"article":{"title":"Envelope check","description":"d","body":"b","tagList":["t"]}}'
$r.article.slug    # before: property does not exist · after: envelope-check-<6 chars>
$r.article.body    # still '' until finding #1 is fixed
```
